day1_insight: There's been no rain at all lately, so stormwater runoff isn't a factor right now. The model's main signals right now: high tide timing is raising risk — how long before mid-morning the last high tide fell, which sets how much the water has just washed off the upper beach; no rain has fallen, so nothing is washing off the land into the surf; and higher waves is raising risk — bigger waves stir up the seabed and resuspend sediment-bound bacteria. The last lab sample (20 MPN/100mL) is now 8 days old — beaches are sampled about weekly, so a reading this stale carries little weight, and this estimate leans on current conditions.
day2_insight: A little recent rain (3.9 mm) may be carrying some runoff to the shoreline — a modest upward pressure on bacteria. The model's main signals right now: high tide timing is raising risk — how long before mid-morning the last high tide fell, which sets how much the water has just washed off the upper beach; high tide level is lowering risk — a high tide can mobilize bacteria held in wet sand and push the waterline toward outfalls; and higher waves is raising risk — bigger waves stir up the seabed and resuspend sediment-bound bacteria. The most recent sample, 7 days ago, was excellent at 20 MPN/100mL.
day3_insight: Recent rain (5.1 mm over the past few days) is washing urban runoff into the surf — the single biggest cause of beach contamination — especially near storm drains and creek mouths. The most recent sample, 6 days ago, was excellent at 20 MPN/100mL.
